biography.plain_text: Yuri Bortsov was a Russian businessman from Lebedyan who built his fortune in juice production. Working alongside his father Nikolay, the factory director, he became chairman and a major shareholder of Lebedyansky. He participated in the sale of its juice business to PepsiCo and Pepsi Bottling Group, retaining interests in baby food and mineral water.

long_biography.plain_text:
Yuri Bortsov helped rescue Lebedyansky by using his trading company, Consent, to sell the factory’s products and pay its costs when frozen accounts threatened operations. He had already run four shops in his home town after studying automation and electromechanics at Voronezh Polytechnic Institute. Once the debts were repaid, his team moved into the factory’s management.

Bortsov pushed for national expansion, bringing in managers with experience at international consumer-goods companies and developing marketing and distribution beyond the regional market. A Moscow branch supported the company’s wider distribution. Alongside his father’s focus on production, he directed commercial strategy as the business developed brands including Tonus, Ya and Fruktovy Sad.
